Seminar Title:

Baicalein Protects Against DNA Damage Induced Ferroptosis in Diabetic Drosophila melanogaster by Restoring Malvolio–Ferritin–Mediated Iron Homeostasis

Seminar Type:

Departmental Seminar

Department:

Life Science

Speaker Name:

Kalpanarani Dash

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

LS Seminar Hall

Date and Time:

09 Nov 2026 04:00 PM

Contact:

8917529521

Abstract:

Among the diverse pathophysiological complications associated with diabetes, dysregulated iron metabolism remains a critical yet comparatively underexplored aspect. The present findings investigate the mechanism by which a high-sucrose diet induces iron overload in Drosophila, leading to ferroptosis, establishing a novel interrelationship between Type 2 diabetes (T2D) and ferroptosis. T2D flies had oxidative stress, which leads to persistent DNA damage in the gut and brain, activating the DNA damage response kinases tefu and mei-41, an upstream regulator of metal transcription factor (mtf-1). In T2D flies, downregulation of mtf-1 inhibits ferritin. Concurrently, upregulation of the major iron importer protein malvolio further increased ferrous iron. Increased ferrous iron and oxidative stress generate toxic lipid radicals, which are the principal catalysts of ferroptosis. The study further reports baicalein as a potential modulator of diabetes-induced ferroptosis. Baicalein alleviates oxidative stress and reduces iron accumulation, potentially by regulating the mechanisms involved in iron uptake, intracellular trafficking, and storage. Molecular docking and simulation revealed that baicalein has a strong binding affinity with malvolio and ferritin. Binding of baicalein disrupts iron absorption by changing the functionality of malvolio, thereby restricting Fe²⁺ accumulation, and upregulates ferritin, promoting sequestration of iron in ferric form, thereby showing protection against ferroptosis.
